svg.text: Top: one Node 1 reading shown in four windows · bottom: the trap when grouping per day
One point in time, four ways to write it
a Node 1 reading in the table readings
stored as one point in time (UTC)
sent by DBeaver when it connects
the pg library gives a Date
All four are the same point in time, only written differently · the ending +00 or Z = UTC, +07 or +0700 = WIB
The trap when grouping per day · a UTC day only starts at 07:00 WIB
ts::date in a UTC session (psql in the container, backend) puts readings from 00:00–06:59 WIB on October 19: wrong
(ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jakarta')::date puts them on October 20 in any window: right
In DBeaver (a WIB session) ts::date happens to be right; don't depend on the session zone.
